help.display.hd44780_i2c_addr: I2C address of the panel's PCF8574 backpack, in hex. 0x27 and 0x3F cover most modules.
help.display.hd44780_rows: Character rows on the panel — 2 and 4 are the common sizes.
help.display.port: Where the display is attached — the modem's own pass-through, or a named serial device. None leaves the node headless, which is the normal Waypoint setup.
help.dmr.beacons: Sends the DMR Roaming Beacon, which lets radios that support roaming discover this node and move to it automatically.
help.dmr.color_code: DMR's equivalent of a CTCSS tone: a number 0–15 that must match at both ends before traffic is accepted. It keeps neighbouring systems on the same frequency from hearing each other. Most hotspots use 1.
help.dmr.dump_ta_data: Logs Talker Alias data — the sending operator's name and callsign carried alongside voice. Diagnostic; it adds noise to the log without changing what is transmitted.
help.dmr.embedded_lc_only: Sends only the Link Control data embedded in DMR voice bursts, leaving out the separate LC data burst. Some networks and repeaters expect this; leave it off unless yours has told you otherwise. Renders to [DMR] EmbeddedLCOnly.
help.dmr.id: Optional override. Leave blank and the node uses the DMR ID from General → Station Identity. Set it only when this node must log in to DMR with a different ID from the one the other gateways use — a separate hotspot ID, for instance.
help.dmr.self_only: Private accepts traffic only from your own DMR ID, so nobody else can key the node. Public accepts any DMR ID. Private is the usual choice for a personal hotspot. Renders to [DMR] SelfOnly.
help.dmrnet.slot1: DMR carries two independent timeslots on one frequency. Turning slot 1 on lets it carry traffic. On a simplex hotspot both slots are usually enabled and the network decides which to use.
help.dmrnet.slot2: The second DMR timeslot. Most talkgroup traffic on BrandMeister arrives on slot 2, so leaving this off will make the node look silent.
help.dstar.module: The single band letter this node identifies as, e.g. B for 70cm or C for 2m. It must match the module your radio calls, and the Band configured in the D-Star gateway.
help.dstar.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave this off when the node runs its own D-Star gateway, which is the normal setup.
help.dstar.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own callsign, so nobody else can key the node.
help.dstargw.dcs: Enable the DCS reflector protocol (the DCS reflectors).
help.dstargw.dextra: Enable the DExtra reflector protocol (the XRF reflectors).
help.dstargw.dplus: Enable the DPlus reflector protocol (the REF reflectors). DPlus requires registration with a US Trust server.
help.dstargw.dplus_login: Callsign used to authenticate to DPlus reflectors — normally your own, and it must be registered with the US Trust system.
help.dstargw.ircddb_hostname: The ircDDB server that resolves callsigns to routes, e.g. rr.openquad.net. This is what makes callsign routing work.
help.dstargw.ircddb_password: Password issued when you registered with the ircDDB network. Stored on the node and never shown again.
help.dstargw.ircddb_username: Your callsign as registered with the ircDDB network. It must be registered there before routing will work.
help.dstargw.reflector: The reflector this node links to when it starts, e.g. REF001 C. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.dstargw.reflector_reconnect: Whether the node returns to its startup reflector after a period of inactivity, and how long it waits. Never leaves it wherever the last user linked it.
help.dstargw.xlx: Enable XLX reflectors, which bridge D-Star with other modes.
help.fm.access_mode: How a transmission is allowed to open the repeater — on carrier alone, or only with the correct CTCSS tone. Requiring the tone stops unrelated signals keying the node.
help.fm.ctcss: The sub-audible access tone in Hz, e.g. 88.5. Your radio must send the same tone before the node will repeat you.
help.fm.ext_audio_boost: Gain applied to audio arriving from the network. Raise it if the network sounds quiet on the air.
help.fm.kerchunk_time: Seconds you must hold a transmission before the node responds, which stops brief “kerchunks” keying it. 0 turns it off.
help.fm.rf_audio_boost: Gain applied to audio arriving over the air. Raise it if you sound quiet to the network.
help.fm.timeout: Maximum seconds of continuous transmission before the node stops keying — the classic repeater timer that stops a stuck mic holding the channel.
help.general.callsign: Your licensed callsign. It identifies this node on every network it connects to, and is what other operators see in last-heard lists. Changing it re-registers the node with its gateways on Apply.
help.general.duplex: Simplex transmits and receives on one frequency, one at a time — the normal hotspot arrangement. Duplex uses separate RX and TX frequencies and needs hardware that supports it. Setting this wrong stops the node passing traffic.
help.general.id: Your DMR ID (sometimes called a CCS7 ID) — the numeric identity issued with your callsign by radioid.net. This is the node-wide default: DMR, and the YSF, P25, NXDN and M17 gateways, all log in with it unless a mode overrides it.
help.general.location: Free text shown to other operators and on network dashboards, e.g. “Kansas City, MO”. Cosmetic — nothing routes on it.
help.general.power: Transmit power in watts, as reported to the network. This is a declaration, not a control — it tells other operators what you are running, it does not change what the radio actually transmits.
help.general.url: A link to this node's public dashboard, published to networks that show one. Leave blank if the node is not reachable from the internet.
help.history.retention_days: How many days of last-heard and event history the node keeps on disk. 0 keeps it forever. Older events are pruned nightly; a longer window uses more SD-card space.
help.lcd.activity_interrupt: Let radio activity take over the panel as it happens, instead of waiting for the page rotation to come round.
help.lcd.enabled: Drive a physically attached HD44780 character panel. Off by default — the node stays headless and reports status over MQTT instead.
help.lcd.i2c_address: I2C address of the panel's backpack, in hex — commonly 0x27 or 0x3F.
help.lcd.i2c_bus: I2C device the panel is wired to. /dev/i2c-1 is the header bus on every Pi since the B+.
help.lcd.linger_secs: Seconds a page stays on the panel before the next one rotates in.
help.lcd.scroll_speed: How fast text longer than the panel scrolls across it.
help.m17.allow_encryption: Pass encrypted M17 frames through the node. Encrypted transmissions are prohibited on amateur bands in most countries — leave this off unless you are certain of your local rules.
help.m17.can: Channel Access Number — M17's equivalent of a CTCSS tone, 0–15. It must match at both ends. 0 is the common default.
help.m17.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own callsign.
help.m17gw.hang_time: Seconds of silence before the node reverts to its startup reflector.
help.m17gw.revert: Return to the startup reflector after the hang time below.
help.m17gw.startup: The reflector and module this node links to when it starts, e.g. M17-M17 C. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.m17gw.suffix: A short suffix distinguishing several M17 nodes running on one callsign.
help.m17gw.voice: Play spoken announcements when the node links or unlinks.
help.modem.board: Which modem board is fitted. Detection reads the board family off the wire, but several products ship the same firmware — a JumboSpot reports as an MMDVM_HS_Hat — so where the identity string cannot tell them apart, this is where you say which one you have. It changes no generated config; it is what lets Waypoint refuse duplex on a board with one radio, and warn when a saved profile came from a differently-tuned board.
help.modem.dmr_delay: Fine timing adjustment for DMR slot alignment on a duplex repeater, in bits. Leave at 0 unless a repeater is losing slot sync.
help.modem.dmr_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for DMR. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.dstar_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for D-Star. Blank follows TX Level, which is what almost every node should do — these exist for a radio whose deviation differs between modes.
help.modem.fm_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for analog FM. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.nxdn_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for NXDN. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.p25_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for P25. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.pocsag_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for POCSAG paging. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.port: Serial device the MMDVM modem appears as — /dev/ttyAMA0 for a GPIO hat, /dev/ttyACM0 for most USB boards. Use Detect on the Hardware tab rather than typing it: detection asks each candidate port what is on the end of it, so a renumbered USB device is found rather than guessed at.
help.modem.ptt_invert: Whether the PTT line is active-low rather than active-high. Wrong, and the repeater either never keys or never stops. A hotspot ignores this.
help.modem.rf_level: RF output power of a hotspot's ADF7021, 0–100%. A hotspot is a milliwatt-class transmitter — this is the difference between reaching the far side of the house and the far side of the room, not a power amplifier control.
help.modem.rssi_mapping_file: Path to a file mapping the modem's raw RSSI counts to dBm, so received signal strengths are reported in real units. Producing one needs a calibrated signal generator; the default path is where the stack looks for it.
help.modem.rx_dc_offset: DC bias on the receive path, −128 to 127, used to centre the waveform on a full-size MMDVM. A hotspot ignores this entirely.
help.modem.rx_freq_hz: The frequency this node listens on — the frequency your radio transmits to. On a simplex hotspot it matches the TX frequency. Check your national band plan before choosing one.
help.modem.rx_invert: Whether the received signal arrives inverted. A full-size MMDVM can be asked directly — it reports inversion in its calibration replies — which is the one analog setting that does not need test equipment. A hotspot ignores this.
help.modem.rx_level: How hard the modem drives its own receive path, 0–100%. On a hotspot this does nothing — the firmware does not read it. On a repeater board it is set so the received waveform fills the range without clipping.
help.modem.rx_offset: Correction in Hz applied to the receive frequency, compensating for crystal error in the modem. Leave at 0 until you have measured the error — this is calibration, not tuning.
help.modem.tcxo_hz: The modem's reference oscillator, in Hz — 12288000 (12.288 MHz) or 14745600 (14.7456 MHz). Firmware from the 1.5 era onwards reports it, and Detect fills this in from what the modem said. Get it wrong and the radio is detuned rather than broken, which is why nothing here ever guesses one.
help.modem.tx_dc_offset: DC bias on the transmit path, −128 to 127. A hotspot ignores this entirely.
help.modem.tx_freq_hz: The frequency this node transmits on — the frequency your radio listens to. On a simplex hotspot it matches the RX frequency.
help.modem.tx_invert: Whether the transmit signal is inverted before it reaches the radio. Depends on how the radio's modulator is wired. A hotspot ignores this.
help.modem.tx_level: Transmit level, 0–100%. On a hotspot this is the deviation of the 4FSK signal it generates; on a repeater board it drives the radio's audio input and is set for 2.75 kHz deviation with a deviation meter.
help.modem.tx_offset: Correction in Hz applied to the transmit frequency, compensating for crystal error in the modem. Leave at 0 until you have measured the error. On a hotspot one oscillator clocks both paths, so this is normally the same number as the RX offset.
help.modem.uart_speed: Line speed between the host and the modem. 115200 is the MMDVM_HS family's default and is almost always right; Detect fills in whichever speed the modem actually answered on.
help.modem.ysf_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for System Fusion. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modes.dmr: Digital Mobile Radio — the most widely used amateur digital mode, with talkgroups carried over networks like BrandMeister and TGIF.
help.modes.dstar: Icom's D-Star, routing through reflectors and callsign-based gateways.
help.modes.fm: Plain analog FM. It has no gateway of its own — the node simply repeats it.
help.modes.m17: M17 — a fully open, patent-free digital voice mode built on Codec2.
help.modes.nxdn: NXDN, connecting to NXDN reflectors by talkgroup.
help.modes.p25: APCO P25 Phase 1, connecting to P25 reflectors by talkgroup.
help.modes.pocsag: POCSAG paging over DAPNET. Transmits pages rather than voice.
help.modes.ysf: Yaesu System Fusion (C4FM), connecting to YSF reflectors and FCS rooms.
help.nxdn.ran: Radio Access Number — NXDN's equivalent of a CTCSS tone, 0–63. It must match at both ends. 1 is the common default.
help.nxdn.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave off when the node runs its own NXDN gateway.
help.nxdn.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own ID.
help.nxdngw.net_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after network traffic stops.
help.nxdngw.rf_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after you stop transmitting.
help.nxdngw.static: Talkgroups the node links to at startup and stays on. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.nxdngw.voice: Play spoken announcements when the node links or unlinks.
help.p25.nac: Network Access Code — P25's equivalent of a CTCSS tone, written in hex. It must match at both ends. 293 is the common default.
help.p25.override_uid_check: Skip validation of the source ID on incoming traffic. Leave off unless a radio you trust is being rejected.
help.p25.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave off when the node runs its own P25 gateway.
help.p25.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own ID.
help.p25gw.net_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after network traffic stops.
help.p25gw.rf_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after you stop transmitting.
help.p25gw.static: Talkgroups the node links to at startup and stays on. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.p25gw.voice: Play spoken announcements when the node links or unlinks.
help.pocsag.auth_key: The AuthKey issued by the DAPNET portal for your callsign. Stored on the node and never shown again.
help.pocsag.blacklist: Never transmit pages for these RICs, even when the server sends them.
help.pocsag.callsign: The callsign this node authenticates to DAPNET with. It must be registered with DAPNET separately from your radio licence.
help.pocsag.frequency: The paging transmit frequency in Hz. Amateur paging uses specific national allocations — check yours before transmitting.
help.pocsag.server: DAPNET server this node fetches pages from, e.g. dapnet.afu.rwth-aachen.de.
help.pocsag.whitelist: Only transmit pages for these RICs (pager addresses). Leave blank to transmit everything the server sends.
help.station_id.callsign: Identify with a different callsign from your station callsign. Leave blank to track General → Callsign automatically.
help.station_id.enable: Keys your callsign in Morse at a fixed interval, so the node identifies itself without you doing anything. Most licences require periodic identification — in the US, every 10 minutes (§97.119).
help.station_id.time_mins: Minutes between identifications. Set this to your licence's requirement or shorter — 10 minutes in the US. Identification is sent between transmissions, never during one.
help.station_id.tx_level: Loudness of the Morse identification, as a percentage of full deviation. Raise it if the ID is hard to copy, lower it if it is jarring next to voice traffic.
help.update.auto_apply: Install updates automatically when they are found. Updates are health-checked after installing, and roll themselves back if the modem does not come back up.
help.update.channel: Which stream of releases this node follows. Stable is the tested one; the others get changes earlier and with more risk.
help.update.check_enabled: Check the signed Waypoint apt repository for new versions. Turning this off means the node never contacts the update server — you will need to check by hand.
help.update.quiet_window: A daily window during which updates are not installed, so a restart never lands in the middle of your regular operating time.
help.ysf.low_deviation: Use narrow deviation, matching radios set to the narrow C4FM setting. Getting this wrong gives distorted or unreadable audio rather than silence.
help.ysf.mode_hang: Seconds the node stays in YSF after traffic stops, before it will switch to another mode. Longer values favour continuing a YSF conversation over letting another mode in.
help.ysf.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave off when the node runs its own YSF gateway.
help.ysf.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own callsign.
help.ysf.tx_hang: Seconds the transmitter stays keyed after a transmission ends, so a quick reply does not have to re-open the link.
help.ysfgw.aprs: Publish position and status to the APRS network.
help.ysfgw.enable_dgid: Use DG-ID routing, which maps DG-ID numbers set on the radio to different reflectors.
help.ysfgw.fcs_network: Connect to the FCS room network. FCS rooms are a separate system from YSF reflectors, and can be enabled alongside them.
help.ysfgw.inactivity_timeout: Minutes of silence before the node reverts to its startup reflector. 0 disables the revert.
help.ysfgw.revert: Return to the startup reflector after the inactivity timeout below.
help.ysfgw.startup: The YSF reflector or FCS room this node links to when it starts. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.ysfgw.suffix: A short suffix appended to the callsign sent to the network, distinguishing several nodes running on one callsign.
help.ysfgw.upper_hostfiles: Fetch reflector host lists from the alternate upstream source.
help.ysfgw.wiresx_passthrough: Pass Wires-X commands from the radio through to the network, so you can change reflectors from the radio's own menu instead of this page.
help.ysfgw.ycs_network: Connect to YCS servers, which add per-talkgroup routing on top of YSF.
help.ysfgw.ysf_network: Connect to the YSF reflector network.
